content:
Apple's October is going to be very busy, with a number of major hardware and software products set to launch. Here's a roundup of all the new Apple products worth looking forward to in October.

iPhone Duo will go on sale on October 23

The iPhone Duo is confirmed to officially reach users in October. Pre-orders will begin on Friday, October 16, with the first batch of units shipping on October 23.

Apple's first foldable model may be available in limited supply. However, the iPhone Duo will launch simultaneously in multiple countries, which could be a good sign for availability. Apple has stated:

If the iPhone Duo's supply was expected to fall far short of market demand, Apple shouldn't be launching the product simultaneously in close to 100 countries and regions right from the start.

Read more: Apple unveils foldable phone iPhone Duo

Hardware rumours: New Mac, Home products, and iPad mini

Reports indicate Apple has quite a few new hardware products ready to debut in October. We expect a new Mac, Home products, and an upgraded iPad mini. Here's what the rumours say so far:

  • Touchscreen MacBook Pro / Ultra: A redesigned high-end MacBook featuring an OLED display and other upgrades
  • M6 iMac: More powerful processor and new colour options
  • M6 MacBook Pro: Updated model of the 14-inch base MacBook Pro
  • All-new Apple TV 4K: Featuring A19 or A19 Pro processor, Siri AI, and a new Siri Remote
  • HomePad: A brand-new home hub device with a built-in touchscreen
  • HomePod mini 2: More powerful processor, improved sound performance, and other upgrades
  • iPad mini: Featuring OLED display and A19 Pro or A20 Pro processor

Two products stand out as particularly noteworthy: the first touchscreen Mac (possibly named MacBook Pro or Ultra), and the long-awaited home hub "HomePad". The rest are only minor updates to existing models.

Software releases: iOS 27.1 and iOS 27.2, etc.

Apple has confirmed that the iPhone Duo will run iOS 27.1 when it launches in October.

Rumour has it that 27.1 will be a Duo-exclusive version. However, the system update may also be pushed to other iPhones, but will only include bug fixes or security updates, with most new features designed for Apple's foldable phone.

Generally speaking, we expect iOS 27.1 to include more features, but this approach is rather unusual this time, as iOS 27.2 has already begun testing and is also expected to launch in October. Therefore, iOS 27.2 is likely designed for all iPhones, while 27.1 primarily serves the iPhone Duo.

Known new features in iOS 27.2 so far include:

  • Apple TV app's profile feature extended to iPhone and iPad
  • Group FaceTime calls to add Dual Capture dual-camera recording
  • Siri AI to support multiple new languages
  • Apple Music, CarPlay Ultra, etc. may also gain new features

When iOS 27 launched, Apple confirmed that Siri AI "will expand support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish next month." Since this language expansion is included in iOS 27.2, we expect both 27.1 and 27.2 to launch in succession before the end of October.

The iOS 27.2 beta also includes an all-new health application with Apple Intelligence features, but this is expected to be removed from the official version and return in iOS 27.3, launching later this year.

Read more: All new features coming to Apple TV in October
